Subject: RE: Acme MSA redlines — liability for security incidents

Team — I reviewed Acme's redlines (attached) and drafted proposed language and negotiation points. Highlights:

1) Incident-specific cap approach: Acme's "12 months of fees or $5M, whichever is lower" exposes Redwood to outsized risk for larger ARR customers and is asymmetric. We should propose a fixed incident sub-limit expressed as either (a) 12 months of fees (capped at $3M) OR (b) a multiple of monthly recurring revenue (MRR) for the impacted service; pick one.

2) Consequential damages carve-out: Acme's request to preserve certain downstream claims is reasonable, but their redline is overly broad. We should accept a tailored carve-out for third-party claims resulting from data loss only where proven negligence or willful misconduct exists.

3) Security Addendum linkage: We can incorporate the Security Addendum by reference, but must ensure the MSA's liability matrix remains the source of truth — the addendum can define controls and reporting obligations, while the MSA defines financial remedies. To avoid conflicts, add an integration clause: "To the extent of any inconsistency, the Order Form and Security Addendum shall govern with respect to security obligations and incident remedies for that Order Form."

4) Exclusions to the sub-limit: We should resist unlimited carve-outs (e.g., for fines, statutory penalties). Propose to exclude from the sub-limit only (i) third-party forensic costs, (ii) customer-notification costs, and (iii) reasonably documented credit-monitoring for affected end-users, each capped (e.g., $200k aggregate).

Attached: Redwood_proposed_breach-cap-language_20270712.docx

Next steps: Kar this needs you to push back on the "whichever is lower" wording and ask Acme to consider our fixed cap approach. Marissa, be prepared to share expected annual spend so Laura can calibrate the cap. If Acme insists on an exception, we can add an approval path with Exec sign-off.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Tom Delgado <tom.delgado@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jul 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA redlines — liability for security incidents

Laura — thanks for the detailed feedback. A few quick counterpoints from our side:

- The intent behind "whichever is lower" was to ensure smaller pilots don't get exposed to a $5M cap; Acme's legal is comfortable with a hard cap but would prefer $5M as an absolute ceiling for enterprise deals.
- Regarding carve-outs: Acme will not accept a position where we bear the bulk of downstream liabilities absent Redwood's negligence; our customers have contractual obligations that flow down and we need to preserve remedies.
- For the three cost categories you propose excluding from the sub-limit (forensic, notification, credit-monitoring), Acme will accept them if they are reasonably documented and tied to a defined incident response plan in the Security Addendum.

Proposed path forward: Agree high-level framework (incident sub-limit + security addendum integration) and run the specific numeric cap in parallel with procurement (we can put a placeholder in the Order Form: "Incident Cap: TBD — parties agree to mutually acceptable cap not to exceed $5,000,000"). Can you confirm Redwood's appetite for that placeholder approach?

Best,
Sofia

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme MSA redlines — liability for security incidents

Sofia — thanks. Redwood can accept a placeholder in the Order Form with a maximum ceiling of $5,000,000 for enterprise deals, subject to the following guardrails:

- The placeholder will read: "Incident Cap: Parties to agree on incident-specific cap no later than execution of Order Form; in no event shall the cap exceed $5,000,000 for enterprise Order Forms."
- We will retain a standard floor/limit logic: default incident cap = 12 months of fees (calculated on the affected Order Form), capped at $3,000,000 unless Parties agree otherwise in writing and Execs approve any cap above $3,000,000. That preserves our risk controls while allowing room for negotiation for large deals.
- Carve-outs: Redwood accepts limited exclusions for forensic investigation, customer notification, and credit monitoring — each to be documented in Exhibit A (Security Addendum) and capped at $200,000 aggregate.
- Integration language: Include the MSA -> Order Form -> Security Addendum precedence clause as discussed.

If Acme is comfortable, we'll prepare a short redline update and a DocuSign envelope with the Order Form placeholder. Please advise procurement contact to expect a follow-up.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
